title: SUSI Substrate Identity
description:
This ledger defines the engine's constitutional mandates, component
topology, execution model, and release/runtime protocols. It is the source
of truth compiled into the binary at build time (see `susi-gawd-agents build.rs → AlphaSelf`).
The public host contract in `README.md` must stay consistent with this document
and with `susi_paths::ports` / `SusiDaemon` — when they disagree, source wins
and both documents are updated in the same change.
canonical_addressing: Canonical addressing: mandates in this document are cited as `Mandate N` (Pillar I) or `Pillar <N> item N` (Pillars II–IV). Source comments predating this document's current structure used to also cite `Rule N`, `Aspiration N`, and `ENGINE-N` — none of those schemes ever corresponded to this document's current numbering, and no reconciliation table exists. As of 2026-09-18 those stale citations were reconciled across every file that carried them. This happened in two passes, and the first pass's own "zero remain" claim was itself wrong: a case-sensitive sweep found 96 mixed-case `Rule N`/`Aspiration N`/`ENGINE-N` occurrences across 19 files and fixed all of them, but the sweep's own regex only matched `Rule` (not `RULE`), so it silently missed 17 further all-caps `RULE N` occurrences across 10 files — caught and fixed in a second pass once discovered. Combined, every citation was either stripped down to its still-accurate descriptive text (the numbered scheme dropped, the reasoning kept — the large majority) or, in the handful of cases where the reference was verifiably the same concept under a new name, rewritten to its real current citation: `admin.rs`'s and `evolution.rs`'s/`reflex_synth.rs`'s "Motion Rule (Protocol)" citations to `Pillar IV item 3` and `Mandate 20` respectively (two genuinely distinct concepts that historically shared the same name, per Mandate 20's own collision note), and `security.rs`'s/`net_guard.rs`'s exact-title matches to `Mandate 10`/`Mandate 12`. No correspondence was ever invented without a verifiable match — where a plausible-looking old number didn't match a current mandate's substance, the number was dropped rather than guessed. Two test-fixture strings in `amas.rs` containing the literal words "test aspiration 23" (simulated mission-goal text, not code comments) were correctly left untouched by both passes.
citation_drift_note: A related, distinct kind of drift — comments citing `Mandate N` using the *current* terminology with a number that doesn't match this document's actual current mandate at that number — was scoped and fixed separately (`EV-2022920-031`): 5 of 41 such citations were wrong, corrected or stripped the same way.

notes: **`global susi`** — background daemon bound to the host substrate (`~/.susi` / `SusiDirs::substrate_home`), not to a project folder. Owns ports, models, and lock state.
**`susi` CLI** — jailed to the caller's cwd; intents run against that workspace.

**Control plane** — `susi start` / `susi stop` / `susi restart` are deterministic host commands (never natural-language missions). `start` / `restart` wait until ports 9090–9093 answer and print the endpoints.
Polluted `~/.susi/config.json` port fields are ignored; accessors always return the constants above.
Peer scouts must not bind 9092 — only the daemon owns the host-contract UDP port.

foundation_pillars.title: Glass box
foundation_pillars.summary: Mandate 26; traces + blackboard + governance + crown reports + `.susi/receipt_archive.jsonl` (audit-only; truth uses live ledger).

foundation_pillars.title: Zero-config Auto
foundation_pillars.summary: Mandate 44; packs/MCP/models/peers auto-prime (`susi auto`); host installs/keys still gate cloud.

foundation_pillars.title: Pluggable
foundation_pillars.summary: `CapabilityRegistry` + extension packs; end-to-end managed catalogs (`susi models` / `frontier` / `openweight` / `agents` / `frameworks` / `mcp` / `openrouter`).

foundation_pillars.title: Reflexes
foundation_pillars.summary: Wasm under data dir; training threshold from config.

design_principles.title: Autonomous by default
design_principles.summary: Mandate 46; plan and execute via swarm consensus, not step-by-step babysitting. Bare `susi "<intent>"` / `susi automate` dispatches GAWD end-to-end; callers are not prompted for each agent step. (One-time cloud-provider preference prompts are host config, not mission babysitting.) Autonomy stays evidence-gated and governance-first — not unbounded "100% automation."

design_principles.title: Grounded outputs
design_principles.summary: claims checked against tools and workspace state. Mission finals require live `ToolReceipt` citations or other absolute truth sources (`TruthTransformer`); EpistemicAuditor rejects hallucinated paths and failed `EvidenceRecord` trails.

design_principles.title: Traceable reasoning
design_principles.summary: thinking and tool calls are inspectable. Mission reports expose agent interactions + evidence ledger + blackboard in protocol output and persist `.susi/last_mission_trace.json` / `.susi/last_blackboard.json` (hashes/provenance for tools; no secret bodies — Mandate 38); tool receipts also append to `.susi/receipt_archive.jsonl` (hashes/provenance only — not truth authority).

design_principles.title: Concurrency-first
design_principles.summary: Tokio, Rayon, Crossbeam, parking_lot on real hardware. Swarm dispatch uses Rayon work-stealing; daemon/HTTP use Tokio; pulse queue uses Crossbeam `SegQueue`; shared state uses `parking_lot` / DashMap — not single-threaded simulation.

design_principles.title: Rust substrate
design_principles.summary: First-party runtime is Rust (or Wasm from Rust). Non-Rust processes are opt-in managed peers only (Mandate 43) — not a false "100% Rust process tree" claim.

design_principles.title: Zero-config auto
design_principles.summary: Boot auto-primes packs/MCP/models/peers without hand-edited config for the happy path (Mandate 44). Installs and API keys remain explicit gates — not "never configure anything."

design_principles.title: OS layer for AI agents
design_principles.summary: Agent-of-agents substrate on the host machine (Mandate 45) — not a replacement host OS.

mandates.title: No Lies
mandates.imperative: Never lie about what happened. Self-reported status, execution outcomes, test results, and known limitations must always match reality, even when the truth is a failure.

mandates.title: No Hallucinations
mandates.imperative: Never fabricate a fact, API, file, or code reference that wasn't verified by reading it. An unverified claim must be stated as unverified, not asserted.

mandates.title: 100% Bloat Rejection
mandates.imperative: Continuously audit for and eliminate technical bloat (dead code, oversized functions, unjustified `.unwrap()`/`.clone()` density, config/behavior drift) rather than claiming an unverifiable absolute; `BloatAuditor` (`susi bloat-audit`) is the enforcement mechanism, not a formality.

mandates.title: Sub-2ms Client Reflex
mandates.imperative: A *client* (CLI caller, IDE, HTTP/MCP caller) must never be left waiting past 2ms for acknowledgment — this governs the client-facing response, not the total wall-clock time of the work itself; see Mandate 32 for how that's achieved (instant return, streaming, or an async task handle). Internal primitive operations (a lock acquisition, a config read, a hashmap lookup) should stay sub-millisecond, but a multi-agent swarm mission's true completion time is bounded by inference and I/O, not this mandate — measuring end-to-end mission latency against a 2ms ceiling produces guaranteed, meaningless "violation" telemetry on every non-trivial mission and must not be done (see Mandate 26).

mandates.title: Lock-Free Execution
mandates.imperative: Utilize non-blocking concurrency primitives. Blocking thread locks are prohibited in the swarm execution path.

mandates.title: Brutally Honest & Critical
mandates.imperative: Maintain a highly critical evaluation mode for code, architecture, and logic.

mandates.title: Continuous Re-Verification
mandates.imperative: A fact verified once (a file's contents, a config value, a running process's state) can go stale mid-task. Re-check assumptions against current codebase and runtime state before acting on them, especially after any action that could have changed that state.

mandates.title: Epistemic Chain of Truth
mandates.imperative: Source code and empirical runtime results outrank prior training knowledge, memory, or assumption. When they conflict, the freshly-read source or the freshly-run result wins, and prior belief is discarded, not defended. Mission completion requires absolute evidence only: live `EvidenceSession` / `ToolReceipt` citations, compiled binary reads, or native verified receipts — models never certify facts (`TruthTransformer`).

mandates.title: Ultra Professional Standard
mandates.imperative: Keep all code, documentation, and comments professional and technical. Zero filler.

mandates.title: No Secret Leaks
mandates.imperative: Zero tolerance for leaking tokens, credentials, API keys, or sensitive configuration data.

mandates.title: Real Working Code Only
mandates.imperative: No hard-coded mockups or placeholder code. Write functional, production-ready code only.

mandates.title: Hardware Authority
mandates.imperative: Physical hardware capacity is the sole and final limit. Saturate CPU/GPU topologies and prevent OOM proactively.

mandates.title: Daemon Persistence
mandates.imperative: Sustain a continuous, resilient background process bound to the host substrate, owning the hard-contract ports 9090–9093 (GMCP/GEMI/UDP/alias) plus models and lock state. Never silently remap those ports.

mandates.title: Substrate Priming
mandates.imperative: Autonomously provision the highest-ranking open-source neural weights compatible with hardware.

mandates.title: Registry Hot-Reload
mandates.imperative: Validate the dynamic agent registry via timestamp-based audits to prevent stale behavior injection.

mandates.title: Absolute Sovereignty
mandates.imperative: Unconstrained runtime adaptation and structural synthesis driven by empirical swarm intelligence.

mandates.title: Recursive Decomposition
mandates.imperative: Spawn parallel sub-swarms for atomic components, joining results upon convergence.

mandates.title: Mission Persistence
mandates.imperative: Maintain stateful mission checkpoints to allow recovery from interrupted swarms.

mandates.title: Decoupled Messaging
mandates.imperative: Utilize asynchronous messaging primitives (Pub-Sub, Actor/CSP channels) for orchestration.

mandates.title: Alpha-Self Evolution Order
mandates.imperative: Self-modification workflow strictly follows: Motion (the triggering intent) -> Architecture (design) -> Structure (implementation) -> Logic (verification). Not to be confused with the release "Motion Rule" (Pillar IV item 3), a distinct, unrelated CI sequence that happens to share the word "Motion" — the two were previously both called "The Motion Rule," a naming collision that made this document self-contradictory about what "The Motion Rule" means.

mandates.title: Dynamic Intent Resolution
mandates.imperative: Intents resolve dynamically along the Continuous Intent Manifold.

mandates.title: Self-Healing Reflex
mandates.imperative: Autonomously recover from structural pathologies, memory faults, or a *stale susi* process holding a host-contract port (Sovereign Eviction / reclaim). Host-contract ports themselves never randomize or drift to ephemeral alternatives — if a foreign process owns 9090–9093, bind fails closed.

mandates.title: Substrate Purity
mandates.imperative: Protocol-agnostic admission via registries and config — OpenAI-compat / Anthropic / Gemini / Triton engines, MCP (stdio/HTTP), and peer agents (`managed` / `cli` / `openai_chat` / `http` / `a2a`). No static domain logic in core; local Candle remains llama/qwen2 GGUF-scoped.

mandates.title: Eternal Liberty
mandates.imperative: SUSI is licensed under Apache 2.0, in perpetuity, per the terms in `LICENSE` (this is a statement of licensing fact, not a behavioral instruction to follow).

mandates.title: Destructive Command Guard
mandates.imperative: Every code path capable of a destructive filesystem, git, or process operation — not only tool-call arguments passed through `exec_command` — must be checked against `SafetyDetector`'s destructive-command patterns (e.g. `rm -rf /`, `rm -rf ~`) before it runs, and any such operation must additionally require an explicit, unambiguous intent sentinel rather than firing on incidental keyword presence in free-text goal input (see Mandate 41). A destructive-pattern list that isn't wired to every place capable of performing that class of operation is a guard that only looks like one; this was found violated in practice (`AdminAgent`'s uninstall action performed an `rm -rf`-equivalent on `~/.susi` without ever consulting `SafetyDetector`, reachable by any goal string containing the word "remove") and fixed, but the general principle — audit coverage must match capability, not just intent — is the actual mandate.

mandates.title: Glass Box Transparency
mandates.imperative: 100% of reasoning steps, tool calls, and state mutations must be visible through telemetry.

mandates.title: Absolute Accountability
mandates.imperative: Every action must be uniquely identifiable and attributable to a specific genomic reflex.

mandates.title: Async Defaults
mandates.imperative: Default to `tokio` for all non-blocking operations.

mandates.title: Data Parallelism
mandates.imperative: Utilize `rayon` for CPU-bound parallel loops and recursive fork-join partitioning.

mandates.title: Locking Standard
mandates.imperative: Mandatory use of `parking_lot` when atomics are insufficient.

mandates.title: Strict 2-Form Substrate Axiom
mandates.imperative:
The substrate exists in exactly two operational forms:
- **`global susi` (The Background Service)**: The persistent background daemon (`susi.service` / `daemon-start`) bound to `SusiDirs::substrate_home` (`~/.susi`). Manages CPU/GPU saturation, OS environment care, hard-contract network ports (9090 GMCP `/mcp`, 9091 GEMI, 9092 A2A UDP, 9093 GMCP alias), and central model weights (`~/.susi/models`). World-facing HTTP is not jailed to cwd (see Mandate 40 and the Host contract section).
- **`susi` (Unconditionally Jailed to `cwd`)**: The single canonical binary invocation (`~/.susi/bin/susi`), unconditionally jailed to the active working directory (`cwd`). Whether executing standard tasks, `susi admin` commands, or operating in `susi repo` (where `cwd` happens to be `susi`'s own Rust source code), `susi` operates exclusively on the active `cwd` context and stages intent bundles (`susi accept`), while the daemon owns ports, models, and lock state.

mandates.title: Zero-Client-Wait Guarantee (Universal Non-Blocking Interop)
mandates.imperative: `susi` must NEVER keep any client waiting (IDE, CLI, MCP client, HTTP/REST caller, or external agent). Because `susi` is non-blocking and instant by design, all client-facing interactions must return an instant response (<2ms), stream live telemetry continuously, or yield a background task handle immediately. Hard execution leases and cancellation checks must terminate unresponsive operations proactively before client timeouts occur.

mandates.title: Synchronized Substrate Versioning & Self-Priming
mandates.imperative: When `susi` operates on `susi repo`, it must automatically synchronize manifests (`susi admin sync`), recompile binaries, and deploy them to `~/.susi/bin/`. Detecting new binary signatures, `local susi` and `global susi` must automatically hot-reload and align to the current version in lockstep across all environments.

mandates.title: The 3 Innovation Pillars of Excellence
mandates.imperative:
- **`susi swarm`**: Delivers maximum hardware power via lock-free CSP channels and work-stealing parallel agent dispatches across all host CPU/GPU cores (agent-of-agents orchestration).
- **`susi engine`**: Races Candle (llama/qwen2 GGUF) against OpenAI-compatible local/cloud engines (and Anthropic/Gemini/Triton via config) through `CapabilityRegistry` — not a claim of native SafeTensors/ONNX chat weights.
- **`susi models` (+ frontier / openweight / openrouter)**: Provides non-blocking resumable background downloads and a dynamic runtime Hugging Face discovery algorithm for the progressive model ladder, **and** durable end-to-end control planes for curated catalogs — coding/agent cloud models (`susi models`), top 5 frontier reasoning engines (`susi frontier`: Claude Sonnet, GPT-4o/5, DeepSeek-R1/V3, Gemini Pro, Llama 3/3.1), open-weight FOSS-adjacent hosts (`susi openweight` via Ollama/vLLM), and OpenRouter routes (`susi openrouter`). Parallel durable planes manage leading external agents/frameworks (`susi agents` / `susi frameworks`) and MCP servers (`susi mcp`; top ranks Filesystem, GitHub, Context7, Playwright, Sentry + Chrome DevTools). Catalogs load via extension packs (`Mandate 35`); no subscriptions are provisioned implicitly.

mandates.title: Registry + Trait + Config Substrate Pattern ("100% Dynamic Config - Zero Hardcoded Structs")
mandates.imperative: All models, providers, agents, tools, and MCP servers must be integrated via dynamic Traits, lock-free Registries (`DashMap`), and runtime JSON/TOML configuration (`config.json`). Hardcoding static vendor strings or model enums in Rust source code is strictly prohibited. Adding a new model, tool, or provider must be doable 100% via configuration or self-registering traits without editing source code. Concretely: `SusiConfig` (`crates/susi-sandbox/src/manager.rs`) is the reference implementation — its root is a `#[serde(flatten)] DynamicRegistry` (`HashMap<String, Value>`), not a closed struct with named fields, and even its nested typed sub-structs (e.g. `ModelLadderConfigStep`) pair named convenience fields with their own flatten catch-all so an unrecognized key is never silently dropped. Every config-shaped struct — anything read from and, especially, written back to a user-editable JSON file — must follow the same pattern. This is not a theoretical concern: `McpServerConfig`/`McpConfig` (`crates/susi-tools/src/config.rs`) had no flatten catch-all until found and fixed (`EV-2022920-046`) — `auto_configure_server`'s read-modify-write cycle on `mcp_config.json` would have silently deleted any field a user hand-added ahead of susi's own support for it. This does not extend to fixed-shape protocol or internal telemetry structs (JSON-RPC envelopes, hardware/evidence reports) that are not user-editable config surfaces — those are correctly typed and closed. **Exception (Host contract):** public ports 9090–9093 are intentional compile-time constants in `susi_paths::ports` and are not user-overridable — Mandate 35 forbids inventing *vendor/model* hardcodes, not freezing the external client port contract.

mandates.title: Pre-Execution Destructive Pattern Guard
mandates.imperative: `SafetyDetector` (`crates/susi-gawd-agents/src/safety.rs`) audits an action's command text against configured destructive-command patterns and critical-system-path patterns before it is allowed to run. This backs Mandate 25 and is what `SafetyAgent` (Pillar II) enforces.

mandates.title: Governance-First Sequencing
mandates.imperative: In any swarm dispatch, `SafetyAgent` and `SecurityAgent` must clear the goal before any execution-capable agent in the same mission is allowed to run — they never race in the same parallel batch as execution-capable agents, since a destructive or leaking action could otherwise complete before the veto lands. This is a scheduling guarantee, not just a policy statement: governance agents are dispatched and awaited first.

mandates.title: Credential Masking
mandates.imperative: Text that will be persisted to telemetry, audit logs, or any other durable record must have configured secret-token patterns redacted (`SecurityDetector::redact`) before it is written — not merely blocked at the point of an explicit "send this secret" action. Mandate 26 (full telemetry visibility) and Mandate 10 (no secret leaks) both hold: redact the secret, don't suppress the surrounding record.

mandates.title: Exfiltration Prevention
mandates.imperative: `SecurityDetector` audits outbound-shaped action text against configured exfiltration-vector patterns (e.g. suspicious URLs, known exfiltration endpoints) before the action runs, independent of and in addition to the secret-pattern check in Mandate 38.

mandates.title: World-Facing Surface Authentication
mandates.imperative: Any network-facing HTTP surface (GMCP HTTP, GEMI REST, or any future equivalent) must support a required bearer-token check (`api_auth_token`) and a per-client rate limit (`rate_limit_per_minute`), both config-driven and both checked before any route is dispatched except CORS preflight and an unauthenticated liveness probe. The daemon **seeds** a host token on first start (`SusiConfig::ensure_api_auth_token_seeded` → `~/.susi/api_token`); when a token is configured, every HTTP peer (including localhost) must present `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Before seeding, non-loopback peers are denied (fail closed on the wire). A world-facing surface with no way to require authentication is not a theoretical gap — this substrate shipped with exactly that gap until it was found and closed.

mandates.title: Untrusted Input Boundary
mandates.imperative: Goal/intent text and any LLM-synthesized artifact derived from it (a specialist agent's `description`, a tool argument, a blackboard entry) must be treated as adversarial once it can originate from an unauthenticated or external caller. Concretely: (a) a mutating or destructive operation must never fire on incidental keyword presence in free-text goal input — it requires an explicit, unambiguous intent sentinel (the `admin pulse:` prefix convention); (b) any agent profile synthesized by an LLM from goal text must be sanitized (bounded field lengths, `is_core` forced false, governance-checked) before it is persisted or ever fed back into a future mission's prompt, since persisted state becomes part of every subsequent mission that recruits it. This mandate exists because both failure modes were found present in shipped code and fixed; it generalizes the fix so the same class of bug can't recur in a new code path.

mandates.title: Fallible Error Handling
mandates.imperative: Zero `.unwrap()`/`.expect()`/`panic!()` in non-test code, except at a call site carrying a comment stating the specific invariant that makes the panic path unreachable (e.g. "safe: length checked above", "safe: regex is a compile-time literal"). Everywhere else, the fallible path must propagate a real `Result`/`EaiResult` via `?` rather than crash the calling thread — this substrate's daemon and swarm-dispatch paths (Mandate 5, Mandate 13) cannot afford an unrecoverable panic from what should have been a recoverable error. `#[cfg(test)]` code is explicitly exempt: an `.unwrap()` on a known-good test fixture is idiomatic and correct, not a violation — this mandate governs production code paths, not test assertions. This is phrased as a scoped rule rather than a bare "no unwrap, ever" specifically because the latter would be false today (269 call sites existed in `src/` when this mandate was written) and Mandate 1 (No Lies) forbids writing a false claim into this document; this mandate is the target an ongoing triage is converging on, not a claim of present compliance. Four triage batches so far: `EV-2022920-047` (`net_guard.rs` found already fully compliant despite a raw count of 7 — every site inside `#[cfg(test)]`; `reflex_synth.rs` had 3 real non-test sites, 2 fixed and 1 given a justifying comment), `EV-2022920-048` (`qwen2_split.rs` also found already fully compliant despite a raw count of 51; `daemon/server.rs`'s 2 real non-test sites fixed — notably `run_daemon_loop`'s config-load `.expect()`, more severe than a typical unwrap because `panic = "abort"` means it aborted the whole daemon process, not just a thread), `EV-2022920-049` (`agents.rs`'s and `speculative.rs`'s one and two real non-test sites respectively, both verified genuinely safe by construction and comment-justified rather than rewritten), and `EV-2022920-050` (`bloat_audit.rs` found to have zero real sites — its raw count of 42 was almost entirely the tool's own report-label strings describing unwrap/expect/clone counts, not actual calls; `manager.rs`'s 4 real sites are all the same bundled-default-JSON pattern, comment-justified once and referenced from the other three rather than repeated). A fifth batch (EV-2022922-098) checked `.expect(`/`panic!(` across eight more crates (susi-sandbox, susi-gemi, susi-gemi-models, susi-agents, susi-core, susi-gawd, susi-gmcp, susi-gawd-agents) plus re-checked `.unwrap()` in susi-core/susi-agents specifically, and found only 14 real non-test sites total across all of that (not the dozens the earlier "~139 remain" estimate implied for a batch of this size) — 6 already carried a Mandate 42 justification comment (sandbox/manager.rs x5, susi-agents/registry.rs x1), and the remaining 8 (susi-sandbox/extensions.rs x5, susi-core/bus.rs x2, susi-core/truth.rs x1) were verified genuinely safe by construction and given one. Zero open non-test sites remain in those eight crates as of this batch. The old "~139 remain" figure predates this batch, was never re-derived from a full re-grep, and should not be trusted as current — five crates (susi-daemon, susi-gawd-swarm, susi-server, susi-tools, susi-native) have not yet been split into real vs. test-only sites at all, so the true remaining count is presently unknown rather than ~139; the next batch should start there.

mandates.title: Rust Substrate (Not Absolute Polyglot Ban)
mandates.imperative: All SUSI **first-party runtime** — daemon, swarm/governance, truth/evidence, inference router (GEMI), MCP host surfaces (GMCP), CLI control planes, and Wasm reflexes compiled from Rust — must be implemented in Rust (or Wasm produced from Rust). This is **not** a claim that the process tree is 100% Rust: non-Rust programs are allowed only as **opt-in managed peers** behind Rust adapters (`susi agents`, `susi frameworks`, `susi mcp`, `susi openweight`, and similar), never as required core paths for substrate operation. Concretely: (a) no new first-party application source in `.py` / `.ts` / `.js` under the repo (distribution scripts like `install.sh` / `install.ps1` / `build-gpu.sh` are exempt as installer tooling, not runtime); (b) optional external bridges may live as Rust string constants executed via host `python`/`npx`/`uvx`/`docker`/`ollama` only when the operator enables that peer; (c) a bare "100% Rust" mandate is forbidden by Mandate 1 because it would be false while Pluggable (Mandate 34 / foundation Pluggable) deliberately manages foreign ecosystems. Absolute process-tree purity would require dropping those managed peers — a product pivot, not a documentation claim.

mandates.title: Zero-Config Substrate Auto (Not Absolute Zero Config)
mandates.imperative: On daemon and CLI boot, SUSI must **auto-prime** the substrate without requiring a hand-edited `config.json` for the happy path: seed/load extension packs, auto-enable leading MCP servers whose launchers and env keys are already satisfied (honoring prior `susi mcp disable`), auto-prefer the best ready coding/frontier model when none is pinned, auto-prime ready external agents/frameworks into the capability registry, and run `bootstrap_zero_config_substrate` / weight-ladder provisioning when policy allows. Operator **installs** (Node, Docker, Ollama, uv, …) and **credentials** (API keys, tokens) remain explicit gates — never silently purchased, invented, or scraped. Missing gates must be diagnosable via `susi doctor` / `setup` / `susi auto status` (and related control planes), not silent no-ops that look like success. Cloud or paid probes must not run without an opt-in path. A bare "zero config forever / never configure anything" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1: foundation pillar Zero-config Auto already states that host installs/keys still gate cloud, and this mandate is that rule in citable DNA form — not a promise that foreign peers appear with an empty machine.

mandates.title: OS Layer for AI Agents (Not a Host OS)
mandates.imperative: SUSI is the **operating layer for AI agents** on a machine — not a general-purpose host operating system. Concretely the layer means: persistent `global susi` daemon bound to `~/.susi`, fixed host-contract ports 9090–9093, evidence-gated agent-of-agents swarm (GAWD), model/MCP/peer admission and control planes, HMAC audit, Wasmer/Docker sandbox, reflexes, and crown-verifiable Tier S pillars. It runs **on** Linux / macOS / WSL (and Windows via installer), does not replace the host kernel, init, package manager, or desktop, and must never be documented or marketed as "the computer's OS" or a drop-in replacement for Linux/macOS/Windows. Public wording must prefer "OS layer for AI agents" / "agent-of-agents substrate" (as in `README.md` and verified product claims) over unbounded "OS for AI" slogans. Absolute replacement-OS language is forbidden by Mandate 1; this mandate is the citable DNA form of that product boundary.

mandates.title: Autonomous Execution by Default (Not Unbounded Automation)
mandates.imperative: Given an intent, SUSI must **plan and execute via GAWD swarm consensus end-to-end** without prompting the caller for each agent step — bare `susi "<intent>"` and `susi automate <intent>` are first-class autonomous surfaces (design principle Autonomous by default). One-time host configuration (API keys, prefer pins, pack load/unload, MCP enable/disable) is **not** mission babysitting. Autonomy remains **bounded**: Mandate 37 (governance-first Safety/Security before fleet); Truth/Evidence gates so mission COMPLETE requires absolute sources and soft model review is not completion; Mandate 41 (mutating admin actions need an explicit `admin pulse:` sentinel); Mandate 44 (missing installs/credentials fail diagnosably, never silent fake success); operator vetoes (disable MCP, clear prefer) must be honored. A bare "100% automation / no human / no veto / always COMPLETE" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1 — this mandate is autonomy *by default under evidence and governance*, not unbounded autopilot.

components.function: Swarm Master Authority: `susi-gawd-agents` 0.1 (fleet/peers/detectors) + `susi-gawd-swarm` 0.1 (AMA/AMAS/DAG) + `susi-gawd-a2a` 0.1 (`ra2a` wire) + `susi-gawd` 0.5 host/governance facade.
Release orchestration, compliance auditing, and axiomatic pulse ingestion.
Substrate maintenance: Hardware audit, model provisioning, and peak selection.
Substrate self-healing: runs the test-driven evolutionary cycle that is Mandate 20's "Alpha-Self Evolution Order" (not Pillar IV's release "Motion Rule" — see that mandate's naming-collision note).
Persistent background host bound to `~/.susi`; owns host-contract ports 9090–9093 and spawns from `~/.susi/bin/susi`.

steps.title: Pulse Ingestion
steps.imperative: Non-blocking asynchronous listener stages intents in the lock-free `SubstratePulseQueue`.

steps.title: Swarm Synthesis
steps.imperative: GAWD constructs a Dynamic Execution Graph (DAG), recruiting specialists via `NeuralAgentFactory`.

steps.title: Truth Convergence
steps.imperative: Swarm outputs pass `TruthTransformer` absolute-evidence gates (live `EvidenceSession` citations, compiled binary reads, or native verified receipts). Soft model review is not a completion path.

steps.title: The 3 Priming Spheres
steps.imperative:
- **`global susi` Primes `AlphaSelf`**: The background daemon profiles host hardware/OS, provisions model ladder weights, owns host-contract ports 9090–9093, and maintains global evidence ledgers.
- **`susi` Primes `AlphaWorld`**: Unconditionally jailed to `cwd`, `susi` indexes local project files, runs unit test audits, and stages intent bundles (`susi accept`).
- **`susi` Primes `susi repo`**: When `cwd` is the engine's source code, `susi` engages self-evolution, running tests, syncing version manifests (`susi admin sync`), and deploying compiled binaries to `~/.susi/bin/`.

protocols.title: Workspace Purity
protocols.imperative: Absolute isolation of artifacts; all ephemeral state contained in `.susi/`.

protocols.title: Hardware Saturation
protocols.imperative: Build and execution must maximize hardware utilization without exceeding physical limits.

protocols.title: Motion Rule (Release Gate)
protocols.imperative: `susi admin release` (`SusiAdmin::execute_release`) *is* this sequence, not a step within it: `cargo check` (default features + the host's native GPU backend feature, never `--all-features`, since `cuda`/`mkl`/`metal` are mutually exclusive) -> compliance audit -> `cargo test` -> `cargo clippy` (same feature matrix as check) -> ephemeral mission smoke tests -> `susi admin sync` (version manifest sync) -> `git push`. Each step gates the next; a `git push` failure is reported as an error, never silently swallowed. Not to be confused with the unrelated "Alpha-Self Evolution Order" (Pillar I, Mandate 20), which used to share this same "Motion Rule" name.

protocols.title: Conventional Reflex
protocols.imperative: Mandatory use of conventional commit prefixes and zero-emoji policy.

protocols.title: Binary Dominance
protocols.imperative: Prioritize pre-compiled binary deployment with transparent local build fallback.

protocols.title: Auto-Path Injection
protocols.imperative: Installer must inject `.susi/bin` into host environment variables.

protocols.title: Canonical Binary Dynamics & Hot-Reload Protocol
protocols.imperative: A single compiled binary deployed at `~/.susi/bin/susi` (the host-contract path). Invocations in `cwd` capture local workspace context, check `~/.susi/substrate.lock`, and ensure `global susi` owns ports/models without duplicate daemons. Detecting binary signature changes (`binary.hash`), `susi` evicts the stale daemon and hot-reloads `global susi` from the canonical binary automatically.
